title: Expanded logistic-Dirichlet mixture benchmark
status: Scenarios informed by the earlier feasibility pilot; this is not an independent confirmatory study

generating_parameters.gaussian_covariance_definition: Same diagonal variances as corresponding shared-shape LD; matched_gaussian also has its positive off-diagonal covariance, negative_correlation replaces it with -0.65*sqrt(var1*var2)

primary_estimands: Component mean RMSE after minimum squared-distance Hungarian label matching
secondary_metrics: Wall time including all starts and any safeguard
protocol: Save this specification and its hash before fitting. Use fresh independent seeds for all repetitions. Do not choose methods, bounds, starts, or mechanisms using held-out outcomes.
Shared and full LD have exactly matched raw-shape, inverse-scale and scaled-location bounds, solver settings, and three starting densities.

If the best full LD training objective is worse than the fitted shared LD by more than the prespecified tolerance, add one full-model start at the embedded shared fit. Count its cost and retain its results. If even this gives a lower objective, retain the embedded feasible shared parameters as a flagged candidate.

All LD starts receive the same conditional refinement when projected score exceeds gtol, up to the prespecified refinement limit. Retain every finite selected fit regardless of convergence, and report failures without silently removing them.

Package t and skew-normal EM use explicit adapters for the same training KMeans partitions. Skew-normal density and sufficient-statistic arithmetic are vectorized and checked against the installed fmvmm routines. Package DMM uses matched initial parameters through its fitting engine, with its original unconstrained M-step; its statistical family is standard LD, while its feasible shape space and stopping rule differ from the bounded direct baseline.
Simulation observations are used in generated coordinates with no learned preprocessing. Selection among starts uses training likelihood only. Test labels enter only external evaluation.

Fit time counts all model-specific starts and refinements, excluding common KMeans partitions. A separate standalone_fit_seconds includes the upstream shared/DMM fit when its warm start is used. Report both rather than treating a supplied warm start as free.
This is prediction and parameter-mean assessment, not a confidence-interval coverage experiment. Runtime is implementation-specific, not code-neutral. No method is guaranteed to outperform another.
